主要内容: Moderna CEO Stephane Bancel has sold more than $400 million in company stock since the start of the pandemic, according to CNBC's analysis of the company's securities filings. The sales, totaling approximately $408 million, were executed under a SEC rule known as 10b5-1, which allows executives to sell shares at regular intervals to avoid insider trading. Bancel's sales averaged roughly $3.6 million per week since January 2020. Moderna's stock has surged 614% since the company announced it received funding to develop a coronavirus vaccine in January 2020. The company's vaccine, developed in collaboration with the National Institutes of Health and with taxpayer support through Operation Warp Speed, has become the second-most commonly used vaccine in the U.S. after Pfizer, with over 209 million doses administered. Bancel's sales reflect the company's strong stock performance, and his estimated net worth from company equity alone exceeds $5.3 billion. Moderna, which went public in December 2018, reported its first profit last year, with $12.2 billion in revenue from $17.7 billion in vaccine sales. The company is projecting at least $19 billion in vaccine sales this year.
